prompt: A particle's velocity is $v(t) = 3t^2 - 12$ meters per second. Find its acceleration at $t = 2$ seconds, in meters per second squared.
hint: Acceleration measures how fast velocity changes. Which operation on $v(t)$ gives the acceleration?

hints.text: Acceleration measures how fast velocity changes. Which operation on $v(t)$ gives the acceleration?
Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, so $a(t) = v'(t) = 6t$. Substitute $t = 2$ into this acceleration function.
The acceleration is $a(2) = 12$ meters per second squared.

explanation: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity, so the power rule gives $a(t) = v'(t) = 6t$.
Substitute the time $t = 2$ to get $a(2) = 6(2) = 12$ meters per second squared.
Note $v(2) = 12 - 12 = 0$: the particle is momentarily stopped at $t = 2$ but accelerating hard, so it immediately starts moving in the positive direction.

alternativeExplanations.title: Rate of change of velocity
steps: Average acceleration over that tenth of a second: $\frac{1.23}{0.1} = 12.3$ m/s².
Close to the instantaneous $12$ m/s²; shrinking the window would bring it closer still.
